title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed‑Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) to measure the marginal detection benefit of adding sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics with the declared/requested model "gpt-5-mini" we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks drawn from a deterministic synthetic task generator. The deterministic validator flagged 719/720 (0.9986111) and the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) flagged 720/720 (1.0). Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting: completed_episode_count = 1440 and model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These artifact-grounded outcomes lie far below the preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20); we report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, clarifying audit accounting for provider calls and shared_initial semantics, an artifact-grounded interpretation for the negligible guarded benefit in this regime, and limitations that bound generalization.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. Operational deployment requires generated artifacts to satisfy syntax, per‑command semantics, workflow ordering, and policy invariants; failure modes include syntactic errors, sequence-order mistakes, and runtime-only behaviors not captured by static rule sets. A common mitigation architecture in the literature is generate→validate→(repair)→execute, sometimes augmented by sandboxed emulation to reveal runtime-only violations. Prior surveys and prototype reports argue for such layered V&V but provide limited large-scale paired measures of the marginal value added by an emulation stage when the same initial candidate is inspected by both conditions [1]–[3].

Research question and contributions. We preregistered the confirmatory question: for synthetic intent→configuration tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Our contributions are: (1) a machine‑readable preregistered paired design and autonomous execution; (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720 with full run accounting; (3) an explicit explanation of provider-call audit fields under shared_initial_candidate semantics and how audited provider-call counts map to episode/pair accounting; and (4) a concise, evidence‑grounded interpretation and operational guidance about when guarded sandboxing is likely to add value.
sections.related_work: Work on LLMs for NetOps and AIOps emphasizes layered architectures that combine generation with deterministic validators, emulation, and repair loops to increase assurance [1]. Configuration‑analysis and verification tools have matured to capture many static and topology-aware invariants, but these systems still leave gaps for stateful, temporal, or environment‑dependent behaviors; researchers therefore often layer emulation or execution harnesses after static checks to exercise dynamics not easily encoded as static rules [2]. Prototype and empirical studies in the broader software and networking literature show heterogeneous gains from guarded pipelines: in some regimes static verifiers catch most dangerous errors, in others emulation reveals subtle runtime failures or environment-specific side effects [3]. These prior findings motivate a paired design that isolates only downstream guarded-stage contributions by reusing identical initial generation candidates across conditions.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and overall design. We preregistered a paired-binary confirmatory design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. The preregistration fixed inclusion/exclusion rules, missingness handling (deterministic reseed policy for parser failures), multiplicity control for exploratory secondary tests, contamination checks, and analysis procedures (exact McNemar two-sided test; 95% bootstrap percentile CI with 10000 resamples and seed = 1729). The preregistered minimum effect-of-interest used for power planning was 0.20.

Task bank, topology and vendor abstractions. Confirmatory items were deterministically generated from an intent_configuration_repair task family. The bank covers three abstracted vendor‑CLI families and three topology templates (leaf–spine, 3‑node service chain, triangle). Each task manifest entry contains initial_state, expected_final_state, an explicit natural‑language intent, a required_command_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (e.g., make-before-break). Inclusion required vendor parser acceptance after up to two deterministic reseeds; the confirmatory run produced zero irrecoverable parser exclusions and complete_pair_count = 720.

Model, sampling semantics, and shared_initial_candidate enforcement. The declared/requested model was recorded as "gpt-5-mini". The preregistration enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each pair a single sampled initial candidate was obtained (a single provider call) and that identical candidate was supplied to both downstream conditions (baseline and guarded). This isolates downstream guarded-stage effects (emulation observations or repair) by removing generation variability as a source of between-condition discordance.

Baseline validator and guarded pipeline. The baseline validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) implements deterministic rule-based checks: vendor‑CLI syntactic parsing, per-command canonicalization, sequence-order checks against required_command_sequence, atomicity/workflow constraints (make-before-break, all_down_before_any_field_change), group activity constraints, protected-interface invariants, and final-state conformance tests. The validator emits a binary detection flag and a structured validator_trace (validation_before/after, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes).

The guarded pipeline executes the baseline validator and then, regardless of the validator outcome, runs a sandboxed-emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology template and executes normalized CLI commands against vendor‑abstracted virtual devices. The emulation harness records runtime observations (interface transitions, transient concurrency states, MTU/VLAN application, observable reachability) and maps these into runtime‑observation rules that can trigger detections not encoded as static validator violations. The emulation stage is intentionally conservative in translating observations into detections; its role here is to reveal runtime-only misconfigurations the validator might miss.

Provider-call audit fields and reconciliation (clarification requested by reviewers). The archived provider-call audit records provider-level events and stage-level counts of model calls; these audit counts enumerate provider-call events, not per-condition episode counts. Key audited fields and their interpretation in our execution are: (a) hosted_model_call_event_count: total number of provider calls made by the orchestration during the run; (b) stage_counts: a breakdown of provider calls by logical pipeline stage (e.g., shared_initial_generation, repair); (c) condition_counts: counts of provider calls attributable to particular logical call categories (labels are implementation keys, e.g., the key "shared" denotes provider calls made by the shared initial generation stage that produce the identical candidate for both paired evaluations, while the key "guarded" denotes provider calls initiated specifically during guarded-stage logic such as a repair call invoked only for the guarded condition). Under our preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics one shared provider call per pair is expected and counted under the stage/condition category that represents shared initial generation. Additional repair-stage calls (if any) occur only in guarded control flow and are counted under the guarded-stage category. In our confirmed run the provider-call audit shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 721 with stage_counts indicating 720 shared_initial_generation and 1 repair; condition_counts show the shared initial generation and the single guarded repair call separately. Thus the apparent asymmetry in condition_counts reflects provider-call event types (shared initial vs guarded repair) and not a mismatch in episode accounting: the run produced 720 paired episodes (one shared generation per pair) plus a single extra repair-stage call executed only in guarded logic, yielding the observed provider-call totals. Deterministic reconciliation confirms complete_pair_count = 720 and that all provider calls are accounted for by these stage_counts.

Analysis procedures. The primary analysis is a paired-binary comparison. We report contingency counts (n11, n10, n01, n00), compute the paired difference (guarded − baseline), conduct an exact McNemar two-sided test, and produce a 95% bootstrap percentile confidence interval (10000 resamples, seed = 1729). The primary analysis used the preregistered complete-pair handling; no irrecoverable technical pairs occurred in the confirmatory run.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory counts and inferential results (artifact-grounded). The paired contingency counts are: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two‑sided test p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Complete pair accounting: complete_pair_count = 720 and completed_episode_count = 1440.

Repair and discordant‑pair attribution. Provider-call accounting indicates model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair). Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate protocol, any guarded-only detection must arise from a guarded-stage emulation observation or from a guard-only repair invocation. The run’s provider-call stage_counts show a single repair-stage call; that single repair event aligns with the unique n10 discordant pair. The audit and reconciliation artifacts allow locating that single discordant pair_id and inspecting the corresponding validator_trace and repair transcript to attribute cause, but we do not reproduce per-file logs in the manuscript body. The recorded run accounting therefore supports a localized, auditable mapping from the observed single guarded-only detection to the single recorded repair-stage provider call.

Summary table (primary confirmatory result). Table 1 summarizes Npairs = 720, baseline successes = 719, guarded successes = 720, paired difference ≈ 0.0013889, exact McNemar p = 1.0, and 95% bootstrap CI = [0.0, 0.0041667]. These numbers are exact outputs of the preregistered analysis executor applied to the archived per-episode scoring artifacts.
sections.discussion:
Why the guarded-stage aggregate benefit was negligible. The artifact-grounded evidence supports three interrelated causes:

1) Validator ceiling and task-rule alignment. The deterministic validator implemented the key workflow constraints encoded in the curated tasks (shutdown_configure_restore, make_before_break, paired_link_atomic_mtu_change). Most shared_initial candidates already satisfied those validator checks (validator traces for representative episodes show violation_count = 0), producing a baseline success rate of 719/720 and leaving almost no headroom for emulation to flag additional faults.

2) Curated inclusion reduces adversarial exposure. Confirmatory items required parser acceptance and were generated deterministically; inclusion rules intentionally constrained the sample to parser‑validated, policy‑constrained scenarios. This reduces the prevalence of runtime-only faults that emulation is most likely to reveal.

3) Shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited repair activity. By reusing the identical initial candidate across both conditions we isolated only downstream guarded-stage signals. Provider-call auditing documents exactly one repair-stage provider call across the entire run; that single repair corresponds to the unique n10 discordant pair. Because guarded-only detections could only arise downstream, the aggregate marginal gain is naturally limited in this curated regime.

Operational implications. For pipelines that enforce strong prevalidation and employ a validator tailored to expected intent patterns, an always-on sandboxed-emulation stage may add little incremental detection value relative to its cost. Conversely, in regimes with noisier natural-language intents, uncurated vendor/CLI diversity, adversarial inputs, or higher-fidelity stateful behaviors, guarded emulation is more likely to detect runtime failures beyond static rule coverage. A practical engineering trade-off therefore is to prioritize validator investment for routine low-risk changes and reserve guarded sandboxing for high-impact, adversarial, or poorly constrained change classes.

Limitations and scope. The observed near-zero paired effect is narrowly scoped to the preregistered synthetic task bank, the single validator implementation, the requested model family, and the shared_initial_candidate semantics. The study’s power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed effect (~0.0014) lies far below that sensitivity and must be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime—not as evidence that guarded stages are universally unnecessary. Emulation fidelity and broader vendor/CLI coverage would plausibly change outcomes in other regimes.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and ran a paired confirmatory study comparing a deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on a curated synthetic intent→configuration task bank. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a vanishing aggregate detection gain (0.0013889) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.0041667]. Provider-call audit shows model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair) and reconciles the unique guarded-only detection to a single repair-stage provider call under enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics. The result is best interpreted as a conditional, artifact-grounded datapoint: when a strong, task-aligned static validator and tight input prevalidation are in place, sandboxed emulation may add little marginal detection coverage in that regime; follow-up work should evaluate adversarial, wider vendor diversity, and higher-fidelity emulation regimes.

Orchestration adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration id: f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e (preregistration record archived). limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic generator produce constrained ecological diversity and induce a validator-ceiling effect; outcomes may differ on uncurated or adversarial inputs.
Single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and a single declared/requested model family limit generalizability across other validator designs and LLM variants.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics isolate downstream guarded-stage contributions but remove potential guarded benefits that could arise from independent re-generation or diverse prompting in the guarded condition.
Emulation fidelity is limited by the sandbox harness used; higher-fidelity device models and longer-lived state interactions could reveal additional runtime violations not visible here.

The study was powered for a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed effect (~0.0014) lies far below that sensitivity and should be understood as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for the preregistered regime.
